A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIG5-CHAT/PSYCHSTEER study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original classifier evaluations, human evaluations, personality assessments, and reasoning and code benchmark results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds prompting/GPT-4o comparisons and original linguistic analyses of BIG5-CHAT and SODA.

M1.justification: The expert-generator training, PSYCHSTEER logit combination, dataset-generation procedure and SFT/DPO alignment methods are retained. Appendix H explains the existing pipeline and its rationale without introducing a different algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: The corpora and tasks are retained, including PsychGenerator, SODA, BIG5-CHAT, BigFive Essay, personality questionnaires, reasoning benchmarks, and appendix HumanEval/MBPP evaluations. The new LIWC analyses reuse existing dialogue coverage.

E2.justification: Compared with v2 Table 11, v3 Table 12 adds Prompt-Mpi, Prompt-LLM-Description and Prompt-Keywords for both LLaMA sizes, plus GPT-4o instruction- and demonstration-based prompting. These substantially broaden the central personality-assessment comparisons while retaining existing comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces LIWC2015 category-frequency measurements normalized by token count, with corresponding SODA responses as controls. GPT-4o adds questionnaire evaluation configurations. Previously stated training budgets, splits and questionnaire/reasoning metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive linguistic validation beyond v2's length and vocabulary statistics: emotion and detailed LIWC-category comparisons across trait levels and SODA (Tables 18–19). It also examines prompt/questionnaire keyword overlap (Table 13) and supplies generator failure examples (H.1). The pipeline discussion does not establish a new controlled steering ablation.

E5.justification: Appendix I newly reports Welch's t-tests and a stated p=0.05 significance level for high/low emotion-frequency differences, although Table 18 supplies no individual p-values. Existing five-run questionnaire statistics, reasoning standard errors and human-agreement statistics are retained.

E6.justification: Existing results retain their values, but consequential comparisons and linguistic findings are added. In v3 Table 12, new 70B Prompt-Keywords BFI averages are 5.0/1.0 for high/low traits, versus unchanged SFT 5.0/1.3 and DPO 5.0/1.4; lower low-trait scores are preferred. Table 18 adds LIWC negative-emotion values of 426.43 versus 149.37 for high versus low neuroticism.

T1.justification: Equation (1), its logit-combination definitions and scaling parameter are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations are added or revised; the new appendices provide conceptual explanations and empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the claims about the 100,000-dialogue dataset, training outperforming prompting, human-like trait correlations and personality-associated reasoning differences. The new appendix evidence does not revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 qualifies the new description-prompt results by identifying possible questionnaire circularity and favoring Prompt-Inst/Prompt-Demo comparisons. Appendix H adds explanations involving monologue-style repetition and coherence, while Appendix I interprets LIWC patterns as linguistic validation. Existing limitations and reasoning interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 changes the stated code repository and adds a separate Hugging Face dataset link. Table 12's caption and Table 13 document new prompts, including GPT-4o-generated 50-word descriptions. However, H.3 says Prompt-Demo resamples each run, conflicting with fixed demonstrations in retained D.5; an actual experimental change is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds Deng et al. (2024), psychometrics surveys by Dong et al. and Ye et al., and linguistic-personality references by Mairesse et al. and Spitzley et al. These support the added comparisons and analyses without substantially changing the paper's human-grounded research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization remain intact. v3 adds Appendices H–I, expands E.3, introduces a descriptive lead-in for the human-personality connection, and makes limited wording and author-contribution edits.

P2.justification: v3 expands the full personality-results table, adds Tables 13, 18 and 19, and moves v2 Table 14 into the main text as Table 4. All five figures retain their content, with some resizing and reflow. The overall table style and two-column layout remain similar.

improvement.justification: The broader comparator coverage, additional linguistic evidence and explicit prompt/pipeline documentation make v3 easier to scrutinize and reproduce. The gain is limited: the unchanged superiority claim is insufficiently reconciled with Prompt-Keywords matching or exceeding SFT/DPO, LIWC significance reporting omits individual p-values, and demonstration-sampling descriptions conflict. The added evidence nevertheless provides a modest net improvement in assessability.
